title: IntoFocus client dashboard v2
subtitle: Shows how a brand's ecommerce performance shapes which brand AI assistants name, and what to do next. Reading rule: a measured zero is a stored 0 with a run id, a missing reading is no row, and a partial read is a run whose rows_read is below population_count.
sampleNote: Synthetic records for a made-up client named Sample Brand. No real customer, seller, or price data.

domains.name: Client context

domains.name: Product data readings

domains.name: Curated outputs

tables.name: reading_run
tables.purpose: Logs every run that reads data, with how many items it should have read and how many it did, so missing, partial, and zero readings stay distinct.
tables.grain: One row per run of one reading source
tables.refresh: One row per run of any reading job
tables.rowEstimate: ~750 today, grows by about 40 per day
notes: complete: rows_read equals population_count. partial: rows_read is below population_count, or the run hasn't finished (finished_at empty). failed: the run ended without usable rows.
A missing reading is an item with no row in any run. A measured zero is a 0 stored on a row that has a reading_run_id.
Replaces fmic_job_state: the next run's starting point is cursor_end on the latest run for that source.
Unique on workflow_execution_id.

tables.name: listing_offer_reading
tables.purpose: Stores what one Keepa run saw on one Amazon listing: whether Amazon withheld the Featured Offer, the offer price, Amazon's outside benchmark, and who holds the offer.
tables.grain: One row per listing per reading run
tables.refresh: Daily product and seller runs, plus the hourly benchmark pass
notes: Unique on (listing_id, reading_run_id). The current state of a listing is its latest row.

Answers why the Featured Offer is withheld: featured_offer_withheld, offer_price_cents, competitive_external_price_cents, and read_at sit on one row. Join listing_channel_price on the same listing_id where price_cents equals competitive_external_price_cents to find the stored outside price that matches.

Product runs fill the price and Featured Offer fields. Seller runs fill the seller fields and leave price fields empty. An empty field means that run didn't read it; seller_class = not_read means a seller read was due but returned nothing.
Suppressed means featured_offer_withheld is true and offer_price_cents is above competitive_external_price_cents.
